extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners, reexamination clerks, CRU/TC reviewers, and Office legal staff involved in ex parte reexamination
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for preparing, reviewing, and issuing an Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate (NIRC and final certificate), including examiner and clerk checklists, examiner's amendments, claim-status designations, and required attachments (reasons for patentability, forms, drawings, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review conference requirement before NIRC
rubrics_metrics.description: A panel review conference must be held in each instance where a NIRC is about to be issued, unless the NIRC is being issued: (A) following and consistent with a decision by the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences (or court) on the merits of the proceeding; or (B) as a consequence of the patent owner’s failure to respond or take other action where such a response or action is necessary to maintain pendency of the proceeding and, as a result of which failure to respond, all of the claims will be canceled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A panel review conference is not to be held where the proceeding is to be concluded by the cancellation of all claims. The issuance of the NIRC in that instance is essentially ministerial.

rubrics_metrics.name: No amendment after prosecution terminated without petition
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules do not provide for an amendment to be filed in a reexamination proceeding after prosecution has been terminated. 37 CFR 1.312 does not apply in reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amendment, information disclosure statement, or other paper related to the merits of the reexamination proceeding filed after prosecution has been terminated must be accompanied by a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 to have the amendment considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title-change practice during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally the title of the invention will not need to be changed during reexamination. If a change of the title is necessary, the patent owner should be notified of the need to provide an amendment changing the title as early as possible in the prosecution as a part of an Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all of the claims are found to be patentable and a NIRC has been or is to be mailed, the examiner may change the title of the invention only by an examiner’s amendment. Changing the title and merely initialing the change is not permitted in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's amendment may change abstract when claims narrowed
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner’s amendment can be made to change the abstract, where the patent owner’s narrowing amendments during the prosecution of the reexamination have changed the focus of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: where a claim is made more specific during reexamination and the abstract does not focus on the specific limitation now required for all patent claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate issuance when all claims disclaimed
rubrics_metrics.description: If all of the claims are disclaimed in a patent under reexamination, a certificate under 37 CFR 1.570 will be issued indicating that fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of file before publication (preparation checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: In preparing the reexamination file for publication of the certificate, the examiner must review the reexamination and patent files to be sure that all the appropriate parts are completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review should include completion of specific items (IFW Search Notes, IFW file jacket, Bibliographic Data Sheet, Issue Classification IFW form) and other items detailed below.

rubrics_metrics.name: IFW file wrapper Search Notes form completion
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'SEARCHED' and the 'SEARCH NOTES' boxes are to be filled in with the classes and subclasses that were actually searched and other areas consulted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 719.05 for further guidance on search notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: IFW file jacket form completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Check to be sure that the necessary data is included on the IFW file jacket form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'Litigation Review' and 'Copending Office Proceedings' boxes should be completed to ensure that the Office is aware of prior or concurrent litigation and Office proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliographic Data Sheet verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Check to be sure that the data included on the Bibliographic Data Sheet is correct and the blank spaces have been initialed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue Classification IFW form completion
rubrics_metrics.description: The form must be completed to set forth the status of each claim and the final claim numbers. The appropriate information must be included in the 'Issue Classification' box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert current international classification and U.S. classification for both the original classification and all cross-references. Completion is required even if all claims are canceled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select drawing figure and representative claim for Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: An appropriate drawing figure is to be indicated for printing on the certificate cover sheet and in the Official Gazette. In addition, a representative claim which has been reexamined is to be indicated for publication in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection instructions: (A) The broadest claim should be selected; (B) ordinarily designate but one claim on each invention (reexamination: examiner must select only one claim); (C) a dependent claim should not be selected unless the independent claim is also printed; in reexamination, a dependent patent claim may be selected where the independent original patent claim has been canceled; (D) in reissue applications, select the broadest claim with changes or the broadest additional reissue claim. When recording: write claim number clearly in black ink, separate multiple claim numbers with commas, and use renumbered patent claim numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney/agent names printing request procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner desires the names of the attorneys or agents, or law firm, to be printed on the certificate, a separate paper limited to this issue which lists the names and positively states that they should be printed on the certificate must be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mere power of attorney or change of address is not a request that the name appear on the certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner must complete PTO-1516 checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must complete a checklist, form PTO-1516, for the reexamination file which will be forwarded to the Office of Data Management identifying information used in printing the reexamination certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of this form may be obtained from the CRU SPE or TC QAS or their support staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspect title report/assignment discrepancies
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should inspect the title report, or patent abstract of title, in the file and verify proper ownership/assignment information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If title report indicates title in inventors but patent shows assignment to an assignee, telephone patent owner and request a statement under 37 CFR 3.73(b) indicating title is in assignee (i.e., it has not reverted back to the inventors). See MPEP § 320.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination clerk duties before mailing NIRC
rubrics_metrics.description: After examiner prepares the NIRC and attachments and completes the Examiner Checklist PTO-1516, the reexamination clerk will complete the Reexamination Clerk Checklist PTO-1517 and revise/update the files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The clerk should check for proper entry of changes in title, inventor, assignee, continuing data, foreign priority, attorney address, and requester’s address in the reexamination and patent files and the PALM data base. After clerk processing, forward to CRU SPE or TC QAS for review; after approval, mail NIRC and forward proceeding to OPLA and Data Management for printing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone inquiry before canceling all claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to canceling the claims and issuing the NIRC, the examiner should telephone the patent owner to inquire if a timely response, timely appeal, etc., was filed with the Office to ensure a timely response has not been misdirected within the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If patent owner indicates no such filing or cannot be reached, the examiner will proceed to issue a NIRC terminating prosecution. If reached and indicated no timely filing, the attachment to the NIRC will make the telephone interview of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's amendment when canceling all live claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When the proceeding is to be concluded by cancellation of all claims, the examiner will issue a NIRC action, and as an attachment to the NIRC, the examiner will draft an examiner’s amendment canceling all live claims in the reexamination proceeding. In the examiner’s amendment, the examiner should point out why the claims have been canceled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example statements are provided noting failure to timely respond or affirmation by the Board and expiration of appeal time, with citation to 37 CFR 1.550(d) and relevant MPEP sections. Physically cancel live claims by placing brackets around them on a copy printed from file history and scanning into IFW.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of claim status on NIRC and Examiner checklist (multiple dependent claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on treating multiple dependent claims for publication: for NIRC purposes additions of multiple dependency count as new claims, deletions count as canceled claims, and unchanged dependent claims may be designated as confirmed; for the Examiner’s checklist, addition or deletion of a claim of the multiple dependency is viewed as amending the claim because of how claims are printed on the certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate how particular claims are reported as confirmed, amended, canceled, or new on both the NIRC and the Examiner’s checklist, and how claims are printed on the certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: All claims with a substantial new question (SNQ) must have been examined
rubrics_metrics.description: All patent claims for which a substantial new question of patentability has been found must have been examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2243 for further discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: No renumbering of patent claims permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: No renumbering of patent claims is permitted. New claims may require renumbering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2250.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to description and claims must conform to 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j)
rubrics_metrics.description: All amendments to the description and claims must conform to requirements of 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j), including any changes made by Examiner’s Amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a portion of the text is amended more than once, each amendment should indicate all of the changes (insertions and deletions) in relation to the current text in the patent under reexamination. See MPEP § 2250.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art listing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The prior art must be listed on a form PTO 892, PTO/SB/08A or 08B, or PTO/SB/42 (or on a form having a format equivalent to one of these forms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These forms must be properly completed. See MPEP § 2257.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete examiner and reexamination clerk checklists (PTO-1516 and PTO-1517)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner and reexamination clerk checklists PTO-1516 and PTO-1517 must be entirely and properly completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clerical checklist is designed to check examiner's responses. The reexamination clerk should personally review the file before completing an item and ensure related items on both checklists are in agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merging of multiple pending reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple pending reexamination proceedings are often merged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2283.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of copending reissue applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the reexamination proceeding is copending with an application for reissue of the patent being reexamined, the files must have been forwarded to OPLA for consideration of potential merger, with a decision by a Senior Legal Advisor or Special Projects Examiner present in the reexamination file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2285.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for patentability and/or confirmation required for each patentable claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasons for patentability are required for each claim found patentable unless all claims are canceled in the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Box 2 of form PTOL-469 is checked and the reasons are provided as an attachment. Reasons should indicate why the claims found patentable are clearly patentable over the cited patents or printed publications, similar to reasons for allowance in an application (see MPEP § 1302.14). Examiner may use form PTOL-476 or preferred form paragraph 22.16. The examiner may refer to particular portions of the record that clearly establish patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: No issue fee in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no issue fee in reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2233.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims may not be amended or added after patent expiration
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent claims may not be amended nor new claims added after expiration of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2250.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original drawings cannot be physically changed
rubrics_metrics.description: Original drawings cannot be physically changed. All drawing amendments must be presented on new sheets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may have the draftsperson review the new sheets. A draftsperson's 'stamp' to indicate approval is no longer required. See MPEP § 2250.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amended or new claim may not enlarge scope
rubrics_metrics.description: An amended or new claim may not enlarge the scope of the patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2250.

rubrics_metrics.name: If patent expired during reexamination, withdraw amendments and added claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent has expired, all amendments to the patent claims and all claims added during the proceeding must be withdrawn. Further, all presently rejected and objected-to claims are canceled by examiner’s amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2250, subsection III, Amendment after the Patent Has Expired. Examiner’s amendment should include a statement expressly withdrawing amendments if the patent expired during the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for examiner's amendment content and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Where it is necessary to amend the patent to place the proceeding in condition to issuance of a reexamination certificate, the examiner may request the patent owner provide the amendment(s), or the examiner may make the amendments with the patent owner’s approval, by a formal examiner’s amendment. The examiner’s amendment must comply with the requirements of 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j) in amending the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner’s amendment requires presentation of the full text of any paragraph or claim to be changed, with the 37 CFR 1.530(f) markings. The exception in 1.121(g) does not apply to examiner’s amendments in reexamination. The only exception to full text presentation is that an entire claim or paragraph may be deleted by a statement deleting the claim or paragraph without presentation of the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraph 22.06 when examiner's amendment accompanies NIRC
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner’s amendment is prepared, Box 7 of form PTOL-469 is checked, and form paragraph 22.06 is used to provide the appropriate attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 22.06 is the examiner’s amendment accompanying Notice of Intent To Issue Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate; it states that changes made will be reflected in the reexamination certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement and handling of 'Reasons for Patentability and/or Confirmation' attachment and comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasons for patentability must be provided as an attachment to the NIRC (Box 2 of PTOL-469). The reasons may be set forth on form PTOL-476 or using form paragraph 22.16.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any comments by the patent owner labeled 'Comments on Statement of Reasons for Patentability and/or Confirmation' must be submitted promptly to avoid delays and will be placed in the reexamination file without comment, even if the reexamination certificate has already issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submissions after NIRC require petition and reconsideration procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules do not provide for an amendment to be filed in a reexamination proceeding after a NIRC has been issued. Any amendment, information disclosure statement, or other paper related to the merits filed after the NIRC must be accompanied by a petition under 37 CFR 1.182.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the petition is granted, the examiner will reconsider the case in view of the new information and, if appropriate, will reopen prosecution. See MPEP § 2256 for criteria for entry and consideration of an information disclosure statement filed after a NIRC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory content and mailing requirements of ex parte reexamination certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: An ex parte reexamination certificate will set forth the results of the ex parte reexamination proceeding and the content of the patent following the proceeding in accordance with 35 U.S.C. 307 and 37 CFR 1.570.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certificate will: (A) cancel any patent claims determined unpatentable; (B) confirm any patent claims determined patentable; (C) incorporate into the patent any amended or new claims determined patentable; (D) make any approved changes in the description; (E) include any statutory or terminal disclaimer filed; (F) identify unamended claims held invalid on final holding by another forum on any grounds; (G) identify any patent claims not reexamined; (H) be mailed on its date to the patent owner (with a copy to the requester); and (I) identify patent claims dependent on amended claims determined patentable. If a certificate cancels all claims, no further Office proceedings will be conducted regarding that patent or related reissue/reexamination requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination case monitoring and post-NIRC screening
rubrics_metrics.description: All reexamination cases are monitored and reviewed in the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) or Technology Center (TC) by the CRU SPE or TC QAS and support staff to ensure that reexamination-specific practice and procedure have been carried out. A panel review is made prior to issuing Office actions as set forth in MPEP § 2271.01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After a NIRC has been issued and prosecution terminated, all reexamination cases go through a screening process in OPLA for obvious errors and proper preparation prior to issuing the reexamination certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and numbering of ex parte reexamination certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The ex parte reexamination certificate is formatted like the title page of current U.S. patents and titled 'Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate' followed by an ordinal number in parentheses indicating its sequential issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certificate number is the original patent number followed by a two-character kind code suffix: first letter 'B' (pre-2001) or 'C' (on/after Jan 2, 2001), and second letter is the number of the reexamination proceeding (showing how many times patent has been reexamined). Inter partes certificates are numbered in a separate sequence.
